fields.name: identifier
fields.desc: A unique identifier assigned to this observation.

fields.name: basedOn
fields.desc: A plan, proposal or order that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this event.  For example, a MedicationRequest may require a patient to have laboratory test performed before  it is dispensed.

fields.name: partOf
fields.desc: A larger event of which this particular Observation is a component or step.  For example,  an observation as part of a procedure.

fields.name: status
fields.desc: The status of the result value.

binding.description: Codes providing the status of an observation.

fields.name: category
fields.desc: A code that classifies the general type of observation being made.

binding.description: Codes for high level observation categories.

fields.name: code
fields.desc: Describes what was observed. Sometimes this is called the observation "name".

binding.description: Codes identifying names of simple observations.

fields.name: subject
fields.short_desc: Who and/or what the observation is about
fields.desc: The patient, or group of patients, location, or device this observation is about and into whose record the observation is placed. If the actual focus of the observation is different from the subject (or a sample of, part, or region of the subject), the `focus` element or the `code` itself specifies the actual focus of the observation.

fields.name: focus
fields.short_desc: What the observation is about, when it is not about the subject of record
fields.desc: The actual focus of an observation when it is not the patient of record representing something or someone associated with the patient such as a spouse, parent, fetus, or donor. For example, fetus observations in a mother's record.  The focus of an observation could also be an existing condition,  an intervention, the subject's diet,  another observation of the subject,  or a body structure such as tumor or implanted device.   An example use case would be using the Observation resource to capture whether the mother is trained to change her child's tracheostomy tube. In this example, the child is the patient of record and the mother is the focus.

fields.name: encounter
fields.short_desc: Healthcare event during which this observation is made
fields.desc: The healthcare event  (e.g. a patient and healthcare provider interaction) during which this observation is made.

fields.name: effectiveDateTime
fields.desc: The time or time-period the observed value is asserted as being true. For biological subjects - e.g. human patients - this is usually called the "physiologically relevant time". This is usually either the time of the procedure or of specimen collection, but very often the source of the date/time is not known, only the date/time itself.

fields.name: effectivePeriod
fields.desc: The time or time-period the observed value is asserted as being true. For biological subjects - e.g. human patients - this is usually called the "physiologically relevant time". This is usually either the time of the procedure or of specimen collection, but very often the source of the date/time is not known, only the date/time itself.

fields.name: effectiveTiming
fields.desc: The time or time-period the observed value is asserted as being true. For biological subjects - e.g. human patients - this is usually called the "physiologically relevant time". This is usually either the time of the procedure or of specimen collection, but very often the source of the date/time is not known, only the date/time itself.

fields.name: effectiveInstant
fields.desc: The time or time-period the observed value is asserted as being true. For biological subjects - e.g. human patients - this is usually called the "physiologically relevant time". This is usually either the time of the procedure or of specimen collection, but very often the source of the date/time is not known, only the date/time itself.

fields.name: issued
fields.short_desc: Date/Time this version was made available
fields.desc: The date and time this version of the observation was made available to providers, typically after the results have been reviewed and verified.

fields.name: performer
fields.short_desc: Who is responsible for the observation
fields.desc: Who was responsible for asserting the observed value as "true".

fields.name: valueQuantity
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueCodeableConcept
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueString
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueBoolean
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueInteger
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueRange
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueRatio
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueSampledData
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueTime
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valueDateTime
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: valuePeriod
fields.desc: The information determined as a result of making the observation, if the information has a simple value.

fields.name: dataAbsentReason
fields.desc: Provides a reason why the expected value in the element Observation.value[x] is missing.

binding.description: Codes specifying why the result (`Observation.value[x]`) is missing.

fields.name: interpretation
fields.desc: A categorical assessment of an observation value.  For example, high, low, normal.

fields.name: note
fields.desc: Comments about the observation or the results.

fields.name: bodySite
fields.desc: Indicates the site on the subject's body where the observation was made (i.e. the target site).

binding.description: Codes describing anatomical locations. May include laterality.

fields.name: method
fields.desc: Indicates the mechanism used to perform the observation.

fields.name: specimen
fields.desc: The specimen that was used when this observation was made.

fields.name: device
fields.desc: The device used to generate the observation data.

fields.name: referenceRange
fields.desc: Guidance on how to interpret the value by comparison to a normal or recommended range.  Multiple reference ranges are interpreted as an "OR".   In other words, to represent two distinct target populations, two `referenceRange` elements would be used.

fields.name: hasMember
fields.short_desc: Related resource that belongs to the Observation group
fields.desc: This observation is a group observation (e.g. a battery, a panel of tests, a set of vital sign measurements) that includes the target as a member of the group.

fields.name: derivedFrom
fields.short_desc: Related measurements the observation is made from
fields.desc: The target resource that represents a measurement from which this observation value is derived. For example, a calculated anion gap or a fetal measurement based on an ultrasound image.

fields.name: component
fields.desc: Some observations have multiple component observations.  These component observations are expressed as separate code value pairs that share the same attributes.  Examples include systolic and diastolic component observations for blood pressure measurement and multiple component observations for genetics observations.

fields.name: identifier
fields.desc: An identifier for this patient.

fields.name: active
fields.short_desc: Whether this patient's record is in active use
fields.desc:
Whether this patient record is in active use. 
Many systems use this property to mark as non-current patients, such as those that have not been seen for a period of time based on an organization's business rules.

It is often used to filter patient lists to exclude inactive patients

Deceased patients may also be marked as inactive for the same reasons, but may be active for some time after death.
